details.description: Llama 2 13B is Meta's 13-billion-parameter pretrained, auto-regressive transformer language model, part of the Llama 2 family spanning 7B to 70B parameters. Released in July 2023 and trained on 2 trillion tokens of publicly available data (knowledge cutoff September 2022), it is a general-purpose base model for commercial and research use in English, meant to be fine-tuned (for example into a chat model) rather than used directly as an assistant. Meta's own GitHub repository for Llama 2 is now marked deprecated, with development consolidated into newer repositories for later Llama generations.
advantages: Scores 54.8 on MMLU (5-shot), per Meta's model card.
Scores 39.4 on BIG-Bench Hard, per Meta's model card.
Part of a family spanning 7B to 70B parameters trained with the same recipe, giving a range of compute/quality tradeoffs, per Meta's model card.
disadvantages: Pretrained base model, not fine-tuned for chat or instruction-following out of the box.
4,096-token context window, per Meta's model card.
Officially supported for English only; Meta says other languages need developer fine-tuning and separate license compliance, per the model card.
Training data has a knowledge cutoff of September 2022, per Meta's model card.
Meta's dedicated GitHub repository for Llama 2 is now marked deprecated, with development moved to newer repositories, per the repo's README.
use_cases: Base for fine-tuning into chat, instruction-following, or domain-specific models.
General-purpose English text generation and completion.
Research on model behavior, alignment, and fine-tuning techniques.

sources.title: meta-llama/llama: Inference code for Llama models

notes: Catalog's 4,096-token max_input/max_output_tokens match Meta's stated 4K context window for Llama 2, so no conflict. Meta's meta-llama/llama GitHub repo (the original Llama 2 inference repo) is itself marked deprecated in its own README, with development consolidated into newer repositories for later Llama generations; that is a statement about the repo/tooling, not a formal end-of-life notice for the model weights, and the catalog's own deprecation_date is empty.
